$comment: The Promo's anatomy, case by case: the stored node in, the exact markup out.
Hand-authored from ticket 17's class table and ticket 03's Q8 table, and read
by BOTH renderers' suites — the React `view` (bundle-src/test/promo-anatomy.test.tsx)
and the Chameleon template (ticket 09's Python suite). Ticket 17 exists so the
two cannot diverge, and ticket 09's stated test is 'the emitted class list
equals the React view's'; this file is what makes that a test against a FIXED
list rather than against whichever ticket landed first.
`html` is the markup INSIDE the host's block wrapper, on the PUBLIC surface.
The wrapper's own `block block-promo has--block-width--<w>` stamp is the
host's and is not our output (ticket 17, 'arriving for free').
No whitespace between elements: the Plate editable computes
`white-space: pre-wrap`, so an inter-element newline becomes a real line box.
JSX drops it by construction; the server template must strip its indentation.
HOW THE TWO SUITES COMPARE. `html` is exact for the React renderer, up to
attribute ORDER: React writes an 's `src` last on purpose, which is its
implementation detail and not something a fixture shared with a Chameleon
template should encode, so each suite sorts attributes before comparing.
Across renderers the contract is the SKELETON: `html` with every attribute
except `class` removed, text kept. That is what lets ticket 09 emit a real
resolution ladder in the while still being held to the same anatomy.
Each suite derives both forms from this one hand-authored `html`, so there is
no second field to drift.
The editor surface is `html` with every `href` dropped (ticket 08's
canvas-safety rule), and nothing else changed.
`reactOnly` marks the single case where the two renderers legitimately
differ, with the reason. Extended together with both suites or not at all.

cases.name: image-only

cases.name: image-with-scales
cases.note: The realistic post-serialization node: ticket 10's three keys plus the base_path it stamps into every scale entry. The React half emits image_url as a single src by decision (no `sizes` policy is available to it); ticket 09 builds the ladder from image_scales. The two agree on the ANATOMY, which is what the skeleton compares.

cases.name: align-orphaned
cases.note: Ticket 17 rule 1 / Q8 row 7: `left` stored, image later cleared. The modifier carries the EFFECTIVE placement, so it reads `center`; the stored value survives untouched.

cases.name: align-unknown
cases.note: A placement the widget cannot produce falls back, rather than emitting a class no sheet dresses.

cases.name: actions-both-variants
cases.note: Reference case A's actions: a button and a link, in DOM order. No slot class — primary/secondary name appearance, not order, and DOM order gives :first-child to anyone who needs position.

cases.name: variant-absent
cases.note: Ticket 03 Q5: the schema `default` is not a storage guarantee, so both renderers fall back to `button` themselves.

cases.name: variant-unknown
cases.note: An off-list variant is not a third appearance: it falls back to `button`, so the sheet never meets a promo-cta with no variant class.

cases.name: action-label-without-link
cases.note: Q8 row 2: renders nothing. A button that goes nowhere is worse than an absent one.

cases.name: action-link-without-label
cases.note: Q8 row 3: symmetric with row 2. No fallback to the target's Title — that would make the canvas fetch the target just to agree with the server.

cases.name: action-link-fails-screen
cases.note: Q8 row 8, as ticket 08 reconciled it with ticket 17's table: a link that fails the Q7 screen is treated exactly as an absent link, so the action renders nothing. The canvas names it; the public page is silent.

cases.name: card-link
cases.note: Q8 row 4: both labels empty and a card link set, so the whole promo is wrapped. Ticket 17 rule 4 — a WRAPPER, never a root whose tag changes, and never a stretched-link overlay that would make the stylesheet load-bearing for clickability.

cases.name: card-link-on-an-empty-promo
cases.note: Rules 3 and 4 compose: the wrapper is outside the root, so an empty promo keeps its single element inside a wrapper that does have something to do.

cases.name: card-link-orphaned-by-a-label
cases.note: Q8 row 5 and the click rule: ANY action label present means the actions take the clicks and the card link is ignored. Never both — no interactive element is ever nested inside another.
cases.html:

cases.name: card-link-orphaned-by-a-label-that-renders-nothing
cases.note: The harsh corner, and it is deliberate: the click rule is keyed on the LABEL, not on whether the action renders (Q8 row 5 says 'any label set'). A label with no link therefore suppresses the card link AND renders no action, so the promo is not clickable at all — and the canvas says so.

cases.name: card-link-fails-screen
cases.note: Ticket 17's table gates the wrapper on a SCREENED link, so an unfollowable one emits no wrapper rather than a class-bearing anchor with nowhere to go.

cases.name: image-external-url
cases.note: Ticket 10 emits a free-text external URL whole — path_of() would strip the host off it — and nothing is appended, because @@images on an external picture is a guaranteed 404.

cases.name: image-value-is-not-a-picture
cases.note: The image field is a free-text surface in Aurora too (ticket 01), so it is screened as well — relative, http and https only.

cases.name: image-dangling-reference
cases.note: Ticket 10: a reference whose target was deleted yields no image_url at all, so the server draws the no-image layout. The canvas cannot tell that apart from an image picked one second ago and previews it anyway — the one stated divergence, argued in imageSrc's docstring. Editor-only and self-correcting.

reactOnly.why: No server has run behind this node, so imageSrc takes step 2 and previews the raw reference.
